title: API 570 Training in New Orleans: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 570 exam prep for New Orleans piping inspectors: CUI in a wet climate, CML circuits on river refinery units, LOOP and dock links. Self-paced online.
h1: API 570 Piping Inspector Exam Prep for New Orleans and the Lower Mississippi
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors from LaPlace to the Gulf

A refinery on the lower Mississippi is easier to picture as pipe than as towers. Crude arrives through lines from offshore and from the St. James hub, crosses the levee to tank fields, runs through unit after unit on racks, and leaves again as product through dock lines and pipelines. This page is for the inspectors who survey and assess that pipe in Garyville, Norco, Chalmette, Meraux and the chemical plants between them, the UT technicians who take its readings, and anyone working towards the API 570 piping inspector certification.

There is no Atlantis classroom in New Orleans. You prepare for API 570 in a self-paced online course, at your own pace, and an instructor answers your questions along the way. The American Petroleum Institute alone sets eligibility, administers the exam at Prometric test centres and certifies successful candidates; the course is preparation and nothing more, and Atlantis holds no API approval as a training provider.

Where plant piping ends and pipelines begin on the lower river

Few places make the API 570 scope question as concrete as this one. The Louisiana Offshore Oil Port, which Louisiana's transportation department describes as a deepwater port about eighteen miles off Grand Isle, pumps crude ashore through a 48-inch, bi-directional Main Oil Line, past the Fourchon Booster Station, to storage at Clovelly that LOOP puts at more than eighty million barrels. When PBF Energy announced its purchase of the Chalmette refinery, the deal listed a pipeline connection to LOOP through a third-party line, a pipeline to the Empire Terminal, a marine terminal and a clean products truck rack. Upriver, the St. James crude hub ties tank farms operated by Plains and others to pipeline connections serving many refineries.

For a candidate, the lesson is the boundary. API 570 covers in-service process piping, and the owner's documents should show where it ends; pipelines carrying crude or product between facilities usually fall under federal pipeline safety rules instead. Exam questions test scope and definitions, not the federal regulations, but knowing which side of the line a spool sits on tells you which interval and repair rules you will actually use. The pipeline boundary guide covers the reasoning, and the API 570 explainer sets out the code's structure.

Corrosion under insulation in a city with 115 wet days a year

New Orleans averages 63.4 inches of precipitation a year on NOAA's 1991 to 2020 normals, spread over about 115 days of wet weather, and the air stays humid in between. Insulation on a lower-river unit rarely dries out completely once water gets in through a torn jacket, an open termination or a weeping steam trace, and after a hurricane or a long power outage whole runs may have been soaked at once. That is why corrosion under insulation drives a large share of local piping findings, and why API 570 gives it more space than most mechanisms.

The code sets target levels for how much CUI inspection to do on systems with no CUI inspection experience, by piping class. API 570 has long printed them like this; check the table in the edition on your effectivity sheet before relying on the figures:

Piping classFollow-up NDE or insulation removal where insulation is damagedNDE at suspect areas within susceptible temperature ranges
Class 175 percent50 percent
Class 250 percent33 percent
Class 325 percent10 percent
Class 4optionaloptional

Suspect areas are the ones water finds first: penetrations, vents, drains, low points, insulation support rings, damaged mastic and places where steam tracing leaks. API RP 571 defines the temperature band in which carbon steel suffers CUI and a separate, warmer band for external chloride cracking of austenitic stainless steel; learn both from your edition rather than from memory. For the exam you need the mechanism, the extent rules and the inspection approach, not a favourite technology. Further reading: CUI in API 570 and API 510 inspection plans and the CUI detection guide.

Circuits for crude, conversion, renewable and chemical service

EIA's 2026 survey lists catalytic cracking at four of the five lower-river refineries, delayed coking at four and hydrocracking at four, so most of them carry the full range of conversion piping: hot FCC slurry and overhead systems, coker heater outlets and fractionator lines, high-pressure hydrogen and effluent circuits, sour water and amine. Valero's St. Charles refinery at Norco announced an expansion of its alkylation unit in 2019, and alkylation brings acid service piping with its own mechanisms. Next door, Diamond Green Diesel's renewable diesel plant runs circuits built around renewable feeds rather than crude, and Dow's St. Charles Operations at Hahnville adds chemical service in carbon steel, stainless steel and alloy pipe.

The circuit is the unit of thinking in API 570. A circuit groups pipe of similar material and environment, so that its condition monitoring locations (CMLs) tell a single story. Three habits keep a lower-river CML programme honest. Circuits follow corrosion loops and process changes, not line numbers, so a renewable feed line and a crude line are never pooled just because they share a rack. CMLs go where the mechanism will show first: elbow extrados in erosive service, the bottom of lines that carry water, downstream of control valves and mix points. And every CML keeps its reason in the record, so that the inspector who reads it in twenty years knows why it was placed there. API RP 574, normally part of the Body of Knowledge, describes the practice; the API 574 explainer summarises it.

Worked example: four CMLs, one circuit, one interval

Take a hypothetical Class 2 hydrocarbon circuit in NPS 6 carbon steel on a Norco-area unit, with a required thickness of 0.180 in. Four CMLs were read in 2021 and again in 2026, five years apart:

CML2021 reading (in.)2026 reading (in.)Rate (in./yr)Remaining life (years)
1, elbow extrados0.2620.2470.003022.3
2, straight run0.2700.2660.0008107.5
3, downstream of a control valve0.2550.2250.00607.5
4, low-point drain0.2680.2510.003420.9

Each rate is the loss divided by five years; each remaining life is (2026 reading − 0.180) ÷ rate. CML 3 governs: 0.045 ÷ 0.0060 gives 7.5 years, half of that is 3.75 years, and Class 2's maximum thickness interval of 10 years is longer, so the circuit's next thickness inspection falls due within 3.75 years. Averaging the four rates to about 0.0033 in. a year would suggest more than 13 years of life at CML 3 and is exactly the shortcut the exam punishes.

The better field answer may be to split the circuit, because loss concentrated just downstream of a control valve points to a local mechanism such as erosion or flashing, not to the general corrosion the other three CMLs show. On small, low-pressure lines, check too whether the structural minimum thickness rather than the pressure design thickness should be the retirement value. The corrosion rate guide covers long-term and short-term rates.

Wet ground, pipe supports and dock lines

Ground behind the levees is low and often saturated, and pipe that dips below grade at a road crossing, a dike wall or a tank field manifold meets the soil-to-air interface. API 570 asks for soil-to-air interfaces on buried piping without adequate cathodic protection to be included in scheduled external inspections, and where pipe is uncoated at grade it has long suggested excavating 6 to 12 in. deep to look for hidden damage. Pipe supports and shoes are the other wet spot: water sits in the crevice, paint fails first there, and touch-point corrosion can thin the bottom of a line where no reading is ever taken. Dock lines that run over the river raise the consequence question that classing is meant to answer. See soil-to-air and buried piping for the detail.

Who sits API 570 around New Orleans

  • Unit and area inspectors in the refinery inspection departments, who own circuit files and want the certification behind their signature.
  • UT technicians who take thickness readings on CML programmes for contractors; Atlantis's own UT thickness and corrosion work in New Orleans is one example of that field role, which builds inspection experience as long as you are performing inspection as the code describes it.
  • Offshore hands looking for an onshore role. Port Fourchon says it services over 95 percent of the Gulf's deepwater energy production and that about 15,000 people a month fly from it to offshore locations. Describe offshore piping work on the application as plainly as any other, and API will judge how it counts.
  • Pipefitters and welders, whose repair and construction experience counts toward the total; some take AWS CWI exam prep first.
  • Engineers from programmes such as the University of New Orleans, who qualify after one year of inspection work with a bachelor's degree.

Experience must fall within the last 10 years and be gained while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency, which includes an owner-user inspection organisation. A two-year degree or certificate in engineering or technology calls for two years, one of them in inspection; a high school diploma calls for three; no formal education, five or more. The API 570 certification requirements page has the detail.

Studying API 570 around a river rotation

Lower-river plants run rotating shifts and long turnaround stretches, and contract inspectors can go from idle to twelve-hour days with a phone call. Keep the self-paced course moving in the quiet weeks: API 570's own rules on classes, intervals, CUI, injection points, dead legs and repairs first, then the RP 574 practices and the damage mechanisms, then the ASME B31.3 arithmetic for pressure design thickness, test pressure and blanks. On a busy unit, a short daily look at practice questions keeps the material warm, and the questions you send the instructor are answered from the code text, which teaches where each answer sits.

Open-book speed comes from knowing B31.3's layout: which chapter holds design, where the allowable stress tables are, and where the definitions sit. The ASME B31.3 explainer is a useful map. The exam itself holds 170 questions, 140 scored and 30 unscored pretest items, 110 of them closed-book and 60 open-book, across a 7.5-hour day that includes a tutorial, a 2.75-hour closed-book session, a 45-minute lunch and a 3.75-hour open-book session with the code PDFs on screen. Prometric lists test centres in and around New Orleans for candidates API has accepted, and windows and deadlines are on the exam schedule page.

Sponsoring piping inspectors from a lower-river site

Owner-users and contractors can put a whole piping inspection group through the API 570 course together, with fees quoted on request. Each candidate still applies to API under their own name and record. It helps to match candidates by exam window, to give each one access to real circuit files so that the code's rules attach to familiar pipe, and to check every experience record against API's rules before anyone pays an application fee.

faq.q: Can I attend an API 570 class in person in New Orleans?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in New Orleans, and the course is built for study online at your own pace, with an instructor who answers questions as they come up. That suits candidates on rotating rosters at Norco, Garyville or Chalmette. You attend in person only on exam day, at a Prometric test centre you book once API accepts your application.

faq.q: Does work on crude lines between LOOP and a river refinery count toward API 570 eligibility?
faq.a: It depends on what the line is. Process piping inside a facility is API 570 territory, while pipelines that carry crude between facilities usually sit under federal pipeline safety rules and their own inspection programmes. API judges experience against the piping the code covers, so describe the equipment, the boundary and your role accurately on the application.

faq.q: How much insulation does API 570 expect a site to remove for CUI?
faq.a: API 570 gives target extents by piping class for systems with no CUI inspection history: a share of damaged-insulation areas followed up by NDE or insulation removal, and a share of suspect areas examined within the susceptible temperature range. The owner's inspection plan sets the actual extent and adjusts it as findings build up, so a site with a long CUI record may do more or less than the table suggests.

faq.q: I rotate offshore out of Port Fourchon. Can that experience count?
faq.a: Possibly. API looks for experience in the design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of piping, with at least one year supervising or performing inspection on most routes, gained within the last 10 years for an owner-user or authorized inspection agency. API's rules are written around the equipment and the work, not the location, so describe the offshore systems and your role carefully, and let API decide.

faq.q: Should a New Orleans UT technician take ASNT Level II UT or API 570 first?
faq.a: Most technicians earn their UT certification first, because thickness surveys on CML programmes are how they build the inspection experience API 570 asks for. API 570 then adds the judgement: classing, intervals, CUI extent and repair rules. Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A UT training as well as API 570 exam prep, and the sequence depends on where your experience record stands.

faq.q: Will alkylation or renewable diesel piping appear on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: The exam does not name units or plants. It tests API 570, RP 574, the damage mechanisms listed in RP 571 for your window and the referenced ASME documents. What you learn from acid, hydrogen or renewable service on the job helps you recognise the mechanisms behind a question, but the answer always comes from the code text.

faq.q: Which document will I search most in the open-book half?
faq.a: Candidates usually spend most of the open-book time in ASME B31.3, because thickness, test pressure and blank calculations draw on its formulas and stress tables, with API 570 and RP 574 close behind. Learn the layout of each PDF before exam day, so that you go straight to the right chapter instead of scrolling.

faq.q: Where do New Orleans candidates sit the API 570 exam?
faq.a: At a Prometric test centre. Prometric lists centres in and around New Orleans, and you choose one after API approves your application for a window. The examination is computer-based and in person; nothing goes into the room with you, and the code PDFs for the open-book questions appear on screen.
